Custody
kŭs´tō-dy
n. (a keeping, guardianship, charge; rendering Hebrew pequddah and yad)
Latin custodia, a guarding. In Numbers it is the Levites' charge of the tabernacle's boards; in Esther, the keeper's charge of the king's women.

Biblical Definition

“And under the custody and charge of the sons of Merari shall be the boards of the tabernacle, and the bars thereof, and the pillars thereof, and the sockets thereof, and all the vessels thereof” (Num 3:36). In Persia the maidens were gathered “to the custody of Hege the king's chamberlain, keeper of the women” (Est 2:3), and “Esther was brought also unto the king's house, to the custody of Hegai” (Est 2:8); after her night she “returned into the second house of the women, to the custody of Shaashgaz” (Est 2:14).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines custody as a keeping; a guarding; care, watch, inspection, for keeping, preservation, or security; imprisonment; confinement.

expand to see more

CUSTODY, n. A keeping; a guarding; care, watch, inspection, for keeping, preservation or security.

2. Imprisonment; confinement; restraint of liberty.

3. Defense from a foe; preservation; security.

Key Scripture

Num 3:36 — "And under the custody and charge of the sons of Merari shall be the boards of the tabernacle, and the bars thereof, and the pillars thereof, and the sockets thereof, and all the vessels thereof, and all that serveth thereto,"

Est 2:3 — "And let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, that they may gather together all the fair young virgins unto Shushan the palace, to the house of the women, unto the custody of Hege the king's chamberlain, keeper of the women; and let their things for purification be given them: unto"

Est 2:8 — "So it came to pass, when the king's commandment and his decree was heard, and when many maidens were gathered together unto Shushan the palace, to the custody of Hegai, that Esther was brought also unto the king's house, to the custody of Hegai, keeper of the women."

Est 2:14 — "In the evening she went, and on the morrow she returned into the second house of the women, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the king's chamberlain, which kept the concubines: she came in unto the king no more, except the king delighted in her, and that she were called by name."

Modern Corruption

The Merarites had custody of the boards and the bars, and the church that despises its dull charges has forgotten who carried the tabernacle.

expand to see more

The Kohathites carried the ark; the Gershonites carried the curtains; the sons of Merari had the custody of the boards, the bars, the pillars, the sockets, and the pins — the heaviest, plainest, least sacred-looking load in the camp, and the tabernacle could not stand without a single piece of it. Numbers 3:36 names their charge with the same care it gives the ark, because in the house of God there is no unimportant custody. The church that honours its preachers and forgets its treasurers, its door-keepers, and the men who set up the boards has a Kohathite theology and a Merarite dependence. Esther's custody is the other picture: a Jewish girl in the keeping of a eunuch in a pagan harem, and every hand she passed through was under a hand that the book never names and never lets the reader forget.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew pequddah (H6486), oversight, charge, custody; yad (H3027), hand, custody.

expand to see more

Hebrew pequddah (H6486) — charge, custody; Numbers 3:36, 4:16.

Hebrew yad (H3027) — hand, custody; Esther 2:3, 2:8, 2:14, Genesis 39:4.

Usage

"“Under the custody and charge of the sons of Merari shall be the boards” — no unimportant custody."

"“To the custody of Hegai” — Esther in a hand under a hand."

"“Returned into the second house of the women, to the custody of Shaashgaz” — the harem's routine, and providence in it."
